Parking is available only at Erftstadt railway station, just 100 m from the start and finish area. Certificates can be downloaded online as PDFs and printed. Courses around Lake Donatus; online registration; parking at Erftstadt railway station; start and finish area at the SC Fortuna Liblar sports grounds.

name: Eifelmarathon
description: The Eifel Marathon on June 14, 2026, in Waxweiler offers a varied running event featuring a marathon, ultramarathon, trail race, half marathon, 10 km fitness run, hiking marathon, and children’s race. The routes pass through the scenic Eifel region, with varied elevation and well-equipped aid stations. The start and finish are in Waxweiler, with a shuttle service to the half-marathon start in Hamm. The event is part of the new Mini-Cup Deutschland and offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with medals for all participants.
course_highlights: Marathon course: 42.195 km with 764 m of elevation gain
Ultramarathon: 51.4 km with 983 m of elevation gain, including a scenic loop through the forest
The half marathon starts in Hamm, with a shuttle service, and follows the reservoir and the Prüm River back to Waxweiler
additional: Race bib pickup on Saturday, June 13, 2026, from 17:00 to 19:00, with a pasta party. On race day (June 14, 2026), race bib pickup is from 07:00 to 09:00. The course closes for all races at 16:00. Every participant receives a medal. Aid stations are staffed from 09:30. Shuttle service for the half marathon from Waxweiler to Hamm. Hiking marathon: approx. 30 km on the Eifel Marathon course. Part of Mini-Cup Deutschland, with prize money for participants who complete three races in Germany. Course approx. 30 km (Waxweiler - Hamm - Waxweiler), start at 08:00, course closes at 16:00, aid stations from 09:30, marked course, medal for all participants.

name: Hahner Kitzenhauslauf
description: The Hahner Kitzenhauslauf is a popular running event in the border region of Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands. The natural, hilly and varied courses in the south of Aachen offer runners a challenging and scenic experience. The event has a long tradition and attracts runners from the region and beyond. It is known for its friendly atmosphere and well-organised races.
course_highlights: Natural running courses in the south of Aachen
Hilly and varied terrain
Scenic routes
additional: Courses for Bambini, schoolchildren, the one-tenth marathon and the half marathon; races counting toward the Regio Aachen Laufcup; refreshments, certificates, photos and live results

name: Integrationslauf des VfB Reichenbach
description: The VfB Reichenbach Integration Run in Reichenbach-Steegen is an annual running event that has been part of the municipality’s event calendar since 2016. The run promotes inclusion and integration through sport by overcoming barriers and enabling people to build connections. The event is open to runners of all ages and offers a shared sporting experience in the region.
course_highlights: Fun run in the municipality of Reichenbach-Steegen
Promotes integration and community through sport
Held since 2016, with a break during the COVID-19 pandemic
additional: The event takes place at the sports grounds in Reichenbach-Steegen and promotes a sense of community through sporting activities for all ages.

name: Kirschlauf
description: The Kirschlauf in Kleinfahner, organised by USV Erfurt, is a long-standing race with a history spanning more than 20 years. The 24th edition takes place on 14 June 2026, taking runners along scenic routes with challenging highland trails. The event offers several distances, including a 14-kilometre main race, a 4.5-kilometre fun run, and races for schoolchildren and younger children. The awards ceremony is traditionally conducted by the Thuringian Cherry Queen, and the race is part of the TLV Running Cup.
course_highlights: 14-kilometre main race featuring a scenic highland trail and views across the northern Thuringian Basin
4.5 km fun run with challenging terrain in the Imtal valley
Finish through a cherry orchard above Kleinfahner, with a magnificent view
additional: Race-pack collection from 8:00 a.m. at the event tent by the mill. Late registration is available online from 2:00 a.m. on 13 June and on race day until 30 minutes before the race, with a €5 late-entry fee. Awards ceremonies take place from approximately 9:45 a.m. for the schoolchildren’s races and from approximately 11:30 a.m. for the other races. Registration until 9 June 2026; late registration is available. The route includes a highland trail and finishes in Kleinfahner. Children’s races and Nordic walking are also offered.

name: Melibokuslauf mit 3. Mountainbike-Gipfelsprint
description: The Melibokus Run is a long-standing running and mountain biking event in Alsbach-Hähnlein, taking place for the 55th time in 2026. It offers several running distances, including a half-marathon trail, 10 km and 5 km running trails, and races for children and teenagers. The Mountain Bike Summit Sprint is also held, featuring a challenging course with 450 m of climbing and 130 m of descent over approximately 13.4 km. The running courses have been evaluated by ITRA and offer varied trails through the countryside around the Melibokus. The event is open to runners and mountain bikers; e-bikes are not allowed.
course_highlights: Half-marathon trail covering 21.2 km
Mountain Bike Summit Sprint with 450 m of climbing and 130 m of descent over approximately 13.4 km
ITRA-evaluated running courses with varied trails
additional: Race-pack collection and late registration from 8:00 a.m. at Sperbergrund, 500 m above Bürgerhaus Sonne. The Mountain Bike Summit Sprint starts at 9:00 a.m., the half-marathon at 9:30 a.m., the 10 km run at 9:45 a.m., and the 5 km run at 10:00 a.m. The children’s races start from 11:00 a.m. Gravel bikes are permitted in the Mountain Bike Summit Sprint; e-bikes are not. Results are processed immediately after the race at the Großsporthalle at Melibokusschule. GPX files of the courses are available. Mountain Bike Summit Sprint distance: approximately 13.4 km. Online registration is available, along with GPX downloads. Public transport stops are in Alsbach-Hähnlein. Age restrictions apply to the competitions.

name: Sohrener Sommerlauf
description: The Sohrener Summer Run is a regional running event in Sohren and part of the Hunsrück Running Series. It is organized by TuS Sohren, a local sports club with a variety of departments, making the event community-focused and non-commercial. Two distances are offered: a short 150-meter run and a 10-kilometer road race. The race typically takes place in pleasant summer weather and gives runners from the region a great opportunity to get active.
course_highlights: Part of the Hunsrück Running Series, which features regional road races
Distances: 150 m and 10 km
Organized by the local sports club TuS Sohren
additional: Typical June weather: approx. 23°C, low of 13°C, mostly sunny with an average of 65 mm of precipitation. Events for children and teenagers; registration required. Start/finish nearby. Typical June weather: around 23°C high, 13°C low, 65 mm of precipitation.

name: Handewitter Sommerlauf
description: The Handewitter Summer Run on June 14, 2026, offers a varied running event for the whole region, with distances for every ability level. From the Bambini race to 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km, Nordic walking, relay, half marathon, and wheelchair race, there is something for everyone. The event takes place around the Wikinghalle in Handewitt and stands out for its excellent organization, great atmosphere, and unforgettable finish-line experience. The courses, measured by the DLV, are flat with few elevation changes, making them ideal for beginners and experienced runners alike.

name: Drei-Länder-Lauf
description: The Three-Country Run takes place on 14 June 2026 in Arenshausen and connects the regions of Thuringia, Lower Saxony and Hesse. The event offers various race distances, including 1.2 km, 2 km, 5 km and 13 km, some on loop courses and others as out-and-back runs. In addition to the main races, there is a fun run for preschool children with no timing, as well as Nordic walking as a non-competitive event. The run has a long tradition as a symbol of the region coming together after German reunification.

name: Schackenslebener Hopfenlauf
description: The Schackenslebener Hopfenlauf is a long-standing running event in Schackensleben, about 25 km west of Magdeburg in the Börde district. All distances start and finish at the sports field. The event offers several distances: 400 m for children, 1.4 km for young people, and 6.0 km and 10.8 km for adults. The longer routes pass through the village and the surrounding countryside, with the typically rolling terrain of the Börde region, on roads and paved farm tracks. Drinks, coffee, cake, and grilled food are available, and after the finish there is a raffle with attractive prizes. The Hopfenlauf is part of the Novo Nordisk Landescup and the Elbe-Ohre-Cup.

name: REWE Women´s Run Hamburg
description: The REWE Women’s Run Hamburg is a road race for beginners and ambitious runners in the Elbe metropolis of Hamburg. The event offers a measured 10 km loop course starting and finishing at Ballindamm. In addition to the main race, there is also the REWE Girl’s Run for girls aged 5 to 10 over 1 kilometer. Participants receive a finisher medal and can use showers and changing facilities after the race.

name: Heidenheimer Sparkassen-Stadtlauf
description: The Heidenheim Sparkasse City Run on June 14, 2026, offers a range of races for everyone from beginners to half-marathon runners through downtown Heidenheim. The half marathon follows two nearly identical laps through the city, passing landmarks such as St. Paul’s Church, the city library, and Brenzpark. The event also includes 10 km and 5 km races, as well as races for schoolchildren and toddlers. All participants receive timekeeping with a transponder integrated into their race number and a generous selection of refreshments at the finish.

name: Herzogstadtlauf Straubing
description: The Herzogstadtlauf in Straubing is a traditional popular running event taking place on June 13 and 14, 2026, and welcoming runners of all ages. From the children’s race and various distances to the BMW Half Marathon, the event offers a varied program with attractive routes through the historic city and city park. Alongside the sporting challenge, an extensive program of stage performances and DJ music creates a lively atmosphere. The event promotes community and health and is a highlight of the running calendar in eastern Bavaria.

name: Hohenneuffen-Berglauf mit BW Trail
description: The 37th Hohenneuffen Mountain Run takes place on 14 June 2026 in Linsenhofen, finishing at Hohenneuffen Castle. The main course covers 9.3 km, with approximately 535 metres of ascent and 180 metres of descent. There is also the 24th Student Mountain Run, with various distances and elevation gains, open to children from first grade onward. The start is at the town hall in Balzholz, and the finish is at the kindergarten on Jahnstraße. We look forward to welcoming many runners from near and far.

name: Metropolmarathon
organizer: Laufteam Fürth 2010 und Team Klinikum Nürnberg
description: The Sparkassen Metropolmarathon 2026 will take place on June 13 and 14 in the cities of Fürth and Nuremberg. The running event connects two cities with varied routes, numerous competitions and a colorful supporting program. With around 9,000 participants and 600 volunteers, the Metropolmarathon offers a weekend full of exercise, fun and community. The events range from the marathon and half marathon to 10 km races, Nordic walking, and races for children and young people.

name: Nesselwanger Seenlauf
description: The 1st Nesselwang Lakes Run, presented by Endress+Hauser and organised by Skiklub Nesselwang e. V., is the successor to the former company run and is aimed at people of all ages. The run promotes exercise and community and offers various routes for children, young people, adults and families, including routes suitable for strollers. The start and finish are at the Trendsportzentrum Allgäu. The event welcomes individuals, companies, clubs and running groups.

name: NEW-Citylauf
description: The 25th NEW-Citylauf in Erkelenz on June 14, 2026, is a popular running event that takes runners of all ability levels through the city center. The event offers a sporty, community-focused atmosphere that appeals to both beginners and ambitious athletes. With a varied course and an infectious atmosphere, the NEW-Citylauf is a highlight of the regional events calendar. Participants are invited to enjoy the joy of running together with family and friends.

name: saarBRÜCKENlauf
description: The Saarbrücken Running Group warmly invites you to the saarBRÜCKENlauf, a guided run across (almost) all of the state capital Saarbrücken’s bridges. Two distances are offered: a 10 km loop with 7 bridges and a 20 km loop with 17 different bridges. This is not a race but a social run with groups at different paces, allowing everyone to tackle the challenging route—with ramps, stairs and many changes of direction—together. The run starts at 10 a.m. at the Kulturbiergarten, opposite the Römerbrücke power plant.

name: Sparkassenlauf
description: The Gladbeck Sparkassenlauf is a long-established running event with DLV-certified courses over 1.5 km, 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. The races take runners through Wittringer Wald on a flat, fast loop course featuring paved walking paths, asphalt and a tartan track. All participants receive a personalised race number bearing their name and a finisher’s medal. The event also hosts the district road running championships and offers net times and live timing.

name: Stadtlauf Kappeln Rund
description: The Kappeln City Run is a traditional running event held annually in Kappeln in the Schleswig-Flensburg district. The event gives runners of different ages and ability levels the opportunity to run a varied course through the town and surrounding area. The run is organized by TSV Kappeln and is a popular event for sports enthusiasts from the region. The atmosphere is welcoming and motivating, with a well-organized event and friendly support.

name: TVE-Sommerlauf 2026
description: The TVE Summer Run is a traditional road race organized by Turnverein 1890 Edingen e.V. in Edingen-Neckarhausen. The event offers races for various age groups, from the youngest runners to seniors, with official timing and certificates. The course is measured by the German Athletics Association (DLV) and is eligible for ranking lists. Runners enjoy a varied route along the Neckar, with the start and finish in the stadium.

name: Alfelder Bernd Meyer Staffelmarathon
description: The Alfeld Bernd Meyer Relay Marathon is a long-standing relay marathon taking place on June 14, 2026, in Alfeld (Leine). The event welcomes runners from across the region and is jointly organized by several local running clubs and the City of Alfeld. The course is an approximately 3 km loop, run twice, with the start and finish on the Market Square. Each team consists of 7 runners, who must be registered by name. Timing is electronic, using single-use transponders. In addition to the relay marathon, there is also a children’s run of approximately 700 m.

name: Bad Kohlgruber Schluchtlauf
description: The Bad Kohlgrub Gorge Run is a scenic race in the Alpine foothills that, despite its name, is not a mountain race. The course is gently undulating and consists of 20% asphalt and 80% forest paths. The event takes place at the Sport and Leisure Center at Erle in Bad Kohlgrub and offers free drinks along the route and at the finish. Coffee, cake, food, and drinks are available, and all participants receive certificates, with trophies for the age-group winners.

name: Barsbütteler Volkslauf
description: The Barsbüttel Fun Run is a long-standing running event held every June at the sports field in the Barsbüttel Sports Center. It offers a range of distances from 400 m to 10 km, which are mostly flat and run along paved or firm, sandy farm tracks. Most of the routes pass through the traffic-free Barsbüttel countryside and offer scenic views, particularly the longer 5 km and 10 km routes. Times are measured electronically, and all participants receive a certificate afterward. Food and refreshments are also available for runners and spectators.

name: BORNE TO RUN (48-Stunden-Lauf)
description: BORNE TO RUN is a 48-hour charity run in Unna that presents an extreme challenge to endurance and willpower. Participants are pushed to their limits over long, demanding hours. This race is for runners ready to take on a true test while supporting a good cause.

name: Famberglauf
description: The Famberglauf is a running event held in June in Fambach, organized by SV Schwarz-Weiß Fambach 09 e.V. The program offers four distances: a half marathon of 21.1 km, the 10.9 km Famberglauf, the 5 km Famberg Sprint, and a 1000 m children’s race. The event is aimed at runners of all ages and abilities and has more of the feel of a family-friendly club run than a major competition.

name: h Lauf Reichenau
description: The Reichenau 24-Hour Run is an extraordinary ultrarun on the island of Reichenau, welcoming individual runners as well as teams of six and corporate teams. The event runs around the clock, from Saturday noon to Sunday noon, and tests participants’ endurance and fitness on a prepared course around the Hochwart. The run has established itself as an impressive sporting challenge, attracting both recreational runners and ambitious athletes. The atmosphere is shaped by community spirit and sporting ambition, supported by a runners’ camp and a dedicated organizing team.

name: KarlsruheLäuft 100 Jahre Berufsfeuerwehr Karlsruhe
description: In 2026, the Karlsruhe professional fire brigade celebrates its 100th anniversary with a varied program of events for the whole city. The anniversary includes sporting competitions, historical highlights such as vintage vehicle gatherings and hand-pump fire engine competitions, as well as ceremonies and the Schlosslichtspiele. The events offer fascinating insights into the history and technology of the fire brigade and invite everyone to celebrate and remember.

name: Kirchenkirnberger Wald- und Wiesenlauf
distance_verbose: 10 km, 5 km, 2.8 km, 1500 Meter, 0.45 km, 0.4 km
description: The 3rd Kirchenkirnberger Forest and Meadow Run takes place on June 14, 2026, in Murrhardt. It is a short running event with two distances, taking runners through forest and meadow landscapes. The race offers a pleasant running atmosphere in typical June weather, with mild temperatures and mostly sunny days. Runners of all ages are warmly invited to take part and enjoy the natural surroundings of Murrhardt.

name: Ludwigsluster Schlossgartenlauf
description: The Ludwigslust Palace Gardens Run takes place on June 14, 2026, in Ludwigslust Palace Park and offers runners of all ages a varied selection of courses. Distances range from 2 km for children to 15 km for experienced runners, complemented by 5 km and 10 km walking events. New to the program is a fun run for the youngest children, with no registration or timing required; participants receive an official medal at the finish. This traditional event warmly welcomes beginners and experienced runners alike to enjoy the beautiful park landscape.

name: Ortslauf Wallertheim
description: The Wallertheim Town Run is a traditional running event held annually in Wallertheim and is part of the Wingertscup. A range of distances is offered, from 900 m for children to 10 km for experienced runners, as well as a 5 km walking course. The event is known for its family-friendly atmosphere, electronic timing with transponder technology, and convenient online registration. It welcomes runners of all abilities and offers a shared sporting experience in the beautiful Rheinhessen countryside.

name: 55. Melibokus Lauf
description: The Melibokus Run is a long-standing running event in Alsbach-Hähnlein, taking place for the 55th time on June 14, 2026. The event offers several race distances, including a half-marathon trail, 10 km and 5 km running trails, and a mountain-bike summit sprint. The courses have been evaluated by ITRA and feature varied trails with challenging climbs and beautiful views. Children and teenagers can take part in separate school races over 400 m, 800 m, and 1,500 m. The event is open to runners of all ages and offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with the start and finish in Sperbergrund.

name: VerenaLauf
location: Hausen ob Verena, Tuttlingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany

name: Omloop van Empel
description: The Omloop van Empel is a popular running race held annually in Empel. The anniversary edition attracts around 1,000 participants each year and is known for its sporty, friendly atmosphere. The organizers work hard to make it a wonderful day filled with socializing and sport. Participants and spectators are invited to enjoy this special running experience together.
course_highlights: Various distances for all levels
Friendly atmosphere with music and drinks
Includes children’s races and family activities
additional: Registration for the 10th edition is closed, and all race entries have been allocated. Around 1,000 participants are expected. The organizers encourage people to come cheer on the participants and experience the event’s atmosphere. Running and walking event; registration via inschrijven.nl; start location: Asmunt 3, Empel

name: Běh zámeckým parkem Kravaře
location: Fotbalový stadion, Alejní ulice, Kravaře, Czech Republic
description: Běh zámeckým parkem Kravaře is a running race held mainly on gravel paths through the chateau park, on a flat course. The race takes place at the football stadium in Kravaře and also includes children’s races. It is organized by Prajzský BK Kravaře, which welcomes all runners to this pleasant and friendly event.
course_highlights: The course runs mostly along gravel paths through the chateau park
Flat course
Children’s races
additional: The first category starts at 9:15, and the main category starts at 10:00. The organizer is Prajzský BK Kravaře; the contact person is Jan Ferenz. The race is mixed and takes place in the Moravian-Silesian Region, at the football stadium on Alejní Street in Kravaře. In 2026, the start was at the football stadium on Alejní Street. Price information applies to the 2026 edition and has not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Půlmaraton okolo Prahy 4
description: The Half Marathon Around Prague 4 is a unique individual running event offering a meditative running experience on the varied terrain of an urban trail. The course is approximately 21 kilometres long and follows the perimeter of the Prague 4 district, giving participants the chance to get to know the area as well as assess their own running form. There is no mass start: runners set off individually or in small groups between 9:00 and 10:00, avoiding stress and congestion at the start and on the course. Following a successful debut, the half marathon is being held for the second time and is suitable for anyone who wants to combine athletic performance with an enjoyable experience in both nature and the city.

name: Chaloupecký kros
description: The Chaloupky Cross-Country Race is a traditional running event held in the picturesque surroundings of Chaloupky near Komárov. The race offers two main routes, approximately 8 km and 4 km long, which run along paved roads, forest trails, and meadows. The main race starts at 10:00, giving participants the chance to enjoy a combination of natural beauty and sporting challenge. The race is part of the Brdy Running Cup and is suitable for the general public; there are no children’s categories.

name: Běh na Hraničář
description: Běh na Hraničář is a traditional and prestigious uphill race held in the picturesque setting of the forest amphitheatre by the Úhlava River in Nýrsko. The 5 km route, with 380 metres of elevation gain, passes the ruins of Pajrek Castle and finishes at the summit of Hraničář, offering a wonderful view of Mount Ostrý. The race is part of the Czech Mountain Running Cup and, after a three-year break, has been held again since 2020. After the race, participants must make their own way back to the start.

name: Dobývání Dívčích hradů
description: The Conquest of Dívčí hrady is a 2 km uphill race with an elevation gain of 135 metres, held in Hlubočepy, Prague 5. The race is part of the Běhy do kopců v Praze a okolí series and offers runners the challenge of a demanding climb. The course passes through picturesque terrain with beautiful views, making the race appealing to fans of mountain running and hill running. It is suitable for anyone looking to test their endurance and strength on hilly terrain.

name: Nocny Maraton Kanału Bydgoskiego od 2007r.
description: The Bydgoszcz Canal Night Marathon is Poland’s oldest continuously held night marathon, taking place since 2007. The race is run in the unique nighttime setting of the Bydgoszcz Planty and along the Bydgoszcz Canal’s distinctive historic hydraulic structures: its 18th-century locks. The canal is the oldest inland waterway in Poland. The event attracts runners from across Poland and abroad, offering generous race packs, original medals and T-shirts, and professional timekeeping. It is growing in prestige and is known for its lively atmosphere, live music, and numerous accompanying attractions.
course_highlights: A night race in the setting of the Bydgoszcz Planty
A route along the historic 18th-century locks of the Bydgoszcz Canal
A unique atmosphere with live music and artistic experiences
additional: There are 6 distances. Participants receive original medals, commemorative T-shirts, and generous race packs. Professional electronic timekeeping and race numbers are provided. Live music adds to the event’s appeal for runners and spectators. The event features 6 distances, electronic timekeeping, commemorative medals and T-shirts, and generous race packs. Participants can expect professional course markings and artistic entertainment during the race.

name: TATRA FEST 2026
description: Tatra Fest is a unique mountain festival held in Zakopane, bringing together a variety of outdoor disciplines, including trail running, climbing, cycling, trekking, and family activities. The event includes challenging races along Tatra trails, such as the 68 km Tatra Fest Bieg and the 22 km Tatra Fest Run, offering participants unforgettable experiences amid the Tatras’ picturesque landscapes. The festival attracts both professionals and amateurs, promoting physical activity, connection with nature, and environmental responsibility. The organizers invite everyone to celebrate life and the mountain spirit together.

name: Zawojski Festiwal Biegowy
description: The Zawoja Running Festival is one of the largest sporting events in the region, held amid the picturesque scenery of Babia Góra and the Police Mountain Range. The festival attracts runners from across Poland and abroad, offering a variety of mountain race distances and a unique atmosphere. The event aims to popularize mountain running and promote the beauty of Babia Góra National Park, combining a sporting adventure with an opportunity to discover the region’s natural and cultural wealth.

name: XVII Elbląski Bieg Piekarczyka Mini Bieg Piekarczyka
organizer: Miejski Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Elblągu
description: The 17th Elbląg Piekarczyk Run is an annual running event held in Elbląg, attracting runners to the 5 km and 10 km races, as well as the Mini Piekarczyk Run for children. The event is known for its unique atmosphere of sporting excitement and community, and participants receive exclusive collectible medals. The organizers provide comfortable race-day facilities, including a race office where participants can collect their race packs, a baggage deposit, and sanitary facilities. The race is a great opportunity to enjoy an active day and compete on the city’s scenic routes.

name: Bieg Charytatywny
organizer: Urząd Miejski w Oławie, Stowarzyszenie Ludzi Aktywnych „Biegnij Oławo”
description: The CZTERY PORY ROKU Charity Run – Stage IV is a sporting event held in Oława, in the park by the railway station. Participants can take part in a run of approximately 5 km or a Nordic Walking march along the same route. The event is charitable and coordinated by the „Biegnij Oławo” Association of Active People and the Oława Municipal Office. The race office is open on race day from 09:30 to 10:30, and the start is scheduled for the same day. The event is supported by local partners, and timing is provided by ZmierzymyCzas.pl.

name: Dziki Trail
description: Dziki Groń is a demanding mountain course in the Pieniny Ultra-Trail® series, following hiking and courier routes as well as the pastures of the Little Pieniny Mountains. The race offers scenic views of the Tatras and the Beskid Mountains, with the start and finish at Dietl Square in Szczawnica. The course is intended for experienced mountain runners looking to take on challenging natural terrain. The event is part of the Pieniny Ultra-Trail mountain running festival, which promotes an active lifestyle and the Pieniny region.

name: IV Charytatywny Bieg z Żonkilem
organizer: Zespół Szkół Ekonomicznych im. Gen. Stefana Roweckiego "Grota" w Opolu
description: The 4th Charity Daffodil Run is a sporting event organized by the Gen. Stefan Rowecki “Grot” School of Economics in Opole. The event will take place on June 14, 2026, on Bolko Island by the Laba Café. Participants can take part in a 5 km run, a 2.5 km Nordic walking event, or support the cause without participating. The run is a charity event that promotes physical activity and support for those in need.

name: Suszecki dziki bieg
description: Suszecki Dziki Bieg is a running event organized by the Suszec Municipal Sports Centre, promoting an active lifestyle among children, young people, and adults. The races will take place on June 13–14, 2026, at the Gwaruś Recreation Centre in Suszec. Participants can compete over 5 km, 10 km, and half-marathon (21 km) distances, as well as in races for children and young people. Combined classifications over 5+21 km and 10+21 km, with prizes in kind, are available for the most determined runners. The friendly atmosphere welcomes both recreational and more experienced runners.

name: VIII Rodzinny Festiwal Biegowy o Złotą K...
description: The 8th Family Running Festival for the Golden K takes place in Dobczyce and is organized by the Rozbiegane Dobczyce group, which has brought together runners from Dobczyce and the surrounding area since 2016. This family running event promotes physical activity and the integration of the local community. The festival welcomes all participants, regardless of age or experience level.

name: X Bieg o Złotą Monetę
description: The 9th Charity Run for the Golden Coin in Olsztyn is an annual running event organized by the Future for Children Foundation, which supports sick and disabled children in Warmia and Mazury. The 5 km main race takes place by Lake Ukiel and is suitable for everyone, including first-time runners. The event also features a family picnic and numerous attractions. Taking part is not only a sporting competition, but above all a way to support children in need. The main race is scheduled to start at 16:30, and the scenic course is also accessible to those who prefer walking.

name: Maraton Smolecki
location: Smolec, Kąty Wrocławskie, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland

name: Mrowna Run Grodzisk łączy w biegu
COOL-BEACH-TRAIL Schellbronn
description: The COOL-BEACH-TRAIL Schellbronn is a mountain running and trail running event with a 3.14 km course. The event takes place in the picturesque surroundings of Bad Wildbad and offers runners a challenging and varied route. It is part of the Sauerland Trailrunning Challenge and attracts trail running enthusiasts who want to combine nature with a sporting challenge.

name: Meine Nacht - Kirche laufend erleben
description: The “Meine Nacht” charity relay race is a community running event in Meine, held in support of charitable causes. The event promotes team spirit and sporting commitment in a special atmosphere. Participants experience a varied course through the municipality that strengthens the sense of community.
course_highlights: Relay format for teams
Course through the municipality of Meine
Charity run with a commitment to social causes
additional: Charity run, registration available via the website, event promotes community and spirituality

name: 95. Terrainkurweg Marathon
description: The 95th Terrainkurweg Marathon in Salzgitter is a challenging run on a hilly course with about 150 meters of elevation gain and loss. The route passes through Vöppstedter Forest, by the Liebenburg forester’s lodge, and along the Salzgitter golf course. The event is not an official DLV event and is intended for well-trained runners. Refreshments, including drinks and snacks, are available in a covered room.

name: Unicredit Pražská štafeta RunCzech
organizer: Prague International Marathon, spol. s r.o. (RunCzech)
description: The UniCredit Prague Relay is a traditional relay race organized as part of the RunCzech series and held at Prague Exhibition Grounds. The race gives teams the opportunity to compete in different relay categories and is known for its friendly atmosphere and professional organization. The organizers emphasize fair conditions and support for the running community in Prague and throughout the Czech Republic. The race is part of the wider RunCzech running events calendar, which also includes marathons and half marathons.
course_highlights: Relay race at Prague Exhibition Grounds
Various relay categories, including special categories
Professional organization with support from experienced pacers
additional: The race pack contains everything runners need. Photography is provided by witisi.photo; photos can be pre-ordered during registration or ordered after the race. Relay categories have a dedicated lane marked with RELAY and 2RUN flags. The organizers recommend using the RunCzech mobile app for better navigation and information during the race. The Prague Relay 2027 takes place from June 22 to 24; the specific date listed for this race is June 22, 2027.

name: Kros Otakara Pachmanna
location: Krčský les, Praha 4, Prague, Czech Republic
description: The Otakar Pachmann Cross-Country Race is a 4.4 km race through the beautiful natural surroundings of Krčský les in Prague 4. It is part of the SABZO series and gives runners the chance to enjoy natural terrain and a woodland atmosphere. It is suitable for anyone who enjoys running in nature and wants a sporting challenge in peaceful woodland surroundings.

name: Bolechowo na Sportowo
organizer: Centrum Rozwoju Kultury Fizycznej AKWEN w Czerwonaku
description: Bolechowo na Sportowo, or Active Czerwonak at Night, is a recurring, free sporting event organized by the Center for the Development of Physical Culture in Czerwonak. The event takes place in the evening and combines physical activity with bringing the local community together. It is a long-standing tradition that attracts participants who want to spend time outdoors in a sporting atmosphere. The event is part of the Czerwonak Grand Prix and is held regularly, promoting a healthy lifestyle.
course_highlights: The race takes place in Bolechowo, in the Czerwonak municipality.
The previous recorded edition covered a distance of 5 km.
The event is part of the Active Czerwonak at Night series.
additional: The event is free and takes place in the evening, usually between 19:30 and 22:00. This recurring sporting event is part of the Czerwonak Grand Prix series. No information is available about participant limits, fees, or required equipment.

name: LKZ Firmenlauf
description: The LKZ Company Run is organized by MTV Ludwigsburg together with the Ludwigsburger Kreiszeitung and takes place on June 17, 2026. The 4.5 km course runs around the Ludwig-Jahn-Stadion and MTV Ludwigsburg. Every year, more than 100 companies send several thousand runners, Nordic walkers, and walkers to the event, supported by numerous volunteers. Alongside the sporting competition, fun and a sense of community take center stage, with cool drinks and an after-run party following the race. MTV members can take part free of charge.

name: Sommernachtslauf am Hufeisen
description: The Summer Night Run at Hufeisen is a traditional race in the municipality of Linsengericht, organized by Laufteam Gelnhausen for over 20 years. The event is known for its friendly, family atmosphere and its popularity throughout the Main-Kinzig district. The start and finish area is in the Hufeisen parking lot, set in woodland between the villages of Geißlitz, Großenhausen and Lützel. As part of the Main-Kinzig-Challenge, the race is an established event in the regional race series and offers runners an appealing course in a natural setting.

name: 401. Malá cena Monaka
location: Restaurace Monako, Slatiňany, Pardubický kraj, Czech Republic
description: The Small Monaco Cup is a traditional running race held in Slatiňany in the Pardubice Region. The race is part of the long-standing history of running events organized by the KRB Chrudim club and gives athletes the opportunity to test themselves on interesting courses. It is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to experience a high-quality sporting event in pleasant surroundings.

name: Běh olympijského dne
description: The Olympic Run is a traditional sporting event organized by the Czech Olympic Committee. It takes place as part of Olympic Day on June 17, 2026, in Zlín. The run brings together different generations and levels of runners, from children to adults, and promotes Olympic values such as friendship, fair play, and respect. Participants can choose from shorter and longer routes, and the race is accompanied by sports and educational activities. Entry fees support children’s participation in sports through the Czech Olympic Foundation. The event is open to everyone who wants to enjoy being active and support a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Zlín
description: The Olympic Run in Zlín is a traditional sporting event held at the Youth Stadium. The race offers a classic five-kilometre course on a tartan track for adults, as well as several shorter children’s races. The event supports sports activities for children from socially disadvantaged families, with part of the entry fee donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration takes place online, and the race starts at 18:00, with the start broadcast on Czech Radio.

name: Olympijský běh - Bakov nad Jizerou
location: Bakov nad Jizerou, Central Bohemian Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Bakov nad Jizerou is a traditional race featuring a flat loop that runs partly along a dirt track and a meadow beside the Jizera River, with the final section on an inline skating track. The race is open to adults and children, with children’s races over 500 and 1,000 metres. The 5 km adult race starts at 18:00 and is held under the auspices of Czech Radio. Participants contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation through their entry fees. Online registration is open until 5 June 2026; registration will not be available on site.

name: Olympijský běh - Bedřichov
description: The Olympic Run in Bedřichov is the largest running event in the Czech Republic and kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the country. The race takes place in the picturesque Jizera Mountains, on a 5 km course. The main category starts at 18:00 by the stadium in Bedřichov. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate the spirit of sport and Olympic values.

name: Olympijský běh - Brloh
description: The Olympic Run in Brloh is a popular regional running race held on June 17, 2026. It is open to a wide range of ages, from children to seniors, and offers courses for both adults and children. The adult course is 5 km long and runs through the picturesque village along a stream, with a turnaround point by an oak tree. Children’s races take place on the track around the football field. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Brno
description: The Olympic Run in Brno is a Gold Race taking place on June 17, 2026, on the meadow by the Komec sports complex in Brno-Komárov. The race offers 5 km and 10 km courses for adults, as well as 400 m and 800 m children’s races by age category. The event is part of the Olympic Day celebrations and features a sports program. The main race starts at 18:00 and will be started live on Czech Radio. Registration is available online only until June 5, 2026, and part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Chip timing, a changing room, baggage storage, and toilets are available for participants.

name: Olympijský běh - Budyně nad Ohří
description: The Olympic Run in Budyně nad Ohří is a traditional sporting event held at the T.J. Sokol Budyně nad Ohří tennis courts. The 5.8 km main race runs across fields, through a small forest and over a gentle hill, on a mix of asphalt, field tracks and forest paths. Children can take part in 400 m and 1,000 m races in the safe surroundings of the tennis courts. The event is part of Olympic Day, which promotes sporting values and friendship, and also supports the Czech Olympic Foundation in helping children take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Bystřice pod Hostýnem
location: Městský park Zahájené, Bystřice pod Hostýnem, Zlín Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Bystřice pod Hostýnem is a new addition to the running calendar. It takes place in the picturesque Zahájené town park, which combines nature with an urban atmosphere. The route is mostly on firm park paths, with short sections of slightly unpaved surface, and is suitable for experienced runners as well as families with children. During the race, participants can enjoy greenery, mature trees and peaceful parts of the park, with no significant elevation changes. The event is both a sporting and social gathering, with an accompanying program, refreshments and opportunities to cheer along the course. The entry fee supports the Czech Olympic Foundation, which helps children take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Čelákovice
description: The Olympic Run in Čelákovice is a traditional running race, with its fifth edition taking place in 2026. The event offers two adult distances, 5 km and 10 km, on flat terrain along the Elbe River, with beautiful views and points of interest including the railway bridge, the Chapel of St. Wenceslas, and the courtyard of the Municipal Museum. Shorter children’s races from 200 m to 1,500 m are also available and pass through the Municipal Museum. The start and finish are on the athletics track at the Čelákovice Municipal Stadium. Online registration is open until June 5, 2026, and the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Olympijský běh - Červená Lhota
description: The Olympic Run in Červená Lhota is a traditional race that starts by the fairytale-like Červená Lhota Castle. Runners follow the blue hiking trail through the villages of Samosoly and Pohoří and across the dam of Kardaš Pond, mostly along field and forest paths. The race is ceremonially started with a shot from a historic weapon, and by taking part you support the Czech Olympic Foundation. The race is for adults over 15 and offers a pleasant sporting atmosphere, with refreshments provided by volunteer firefighters.

name: Olympijský běh - Červené Pečky
description: The Olympic Run in Červené Pečky is a new location in the Kolín area, offering a course suitable for beginners too. The adult main race is 4.5 km long and runs 90% over easy terrain around the football pitch and a small local wood, with the remaining 10% on asphalt. Shorter courses adapted to children’s age and ability are available. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation; part of the entry fee goes towards supporting children’s participation in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Česká Lípa
description: The Olympic Run in Česká Lípa is a newcomer to the running map, centered around the renovated U Ploučnice municipal stadium. Runners head towards Holý vrch, the town’s western landmark, then return along the Ploučnice River to the stadium, where the start and finish are located. The event is open to adults and children, with several shorter races for children. The main race starts at 18:00, and online registration is open until 5 June 2026. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Česká Skalice
description: The Olympic Run in Česká Skalice is part of the nationwide Olympic Day event, which celebrates sport and Olympic values such as friendship, fair play, and respect. The race offers routes for adults and children, and every participant contributes part of their entry fee to support children’s sports. The event is open to everyone, regardless of ability, and is an ideal opportunity to enjoy being active together in the beautiful Hradec Králové Region. The Olympic Run brings people and sports together for a day full of sporting activities and Olympic spirit.

name: Olympijský běh - České Budějovice
description: The Olympic Run in České Budějovice is a traditional race for fans of challenging terrain. The 7 km route crosses the U Špačků ford, follows the right bank of the Malše River to Roudné, and returns to the boathouse. The race is open to adults and children, with a separate 1.5 km route for the children’s races. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00 by the Hanace boathouse in České Budějovice.

name: Olympijský běh - Dačice
description: The Olympic Run in Dačice is a traditional sporting event held in the beautiful grounds of the Dačice State Chateau park. The race follows a route mainly along forest and field paths, suitable for adults and children. The event also features an accompanying program, with the option to visit the chateau and the town museum. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation, which encourages children to take part in sport.

name: Olympijský běh - Děčín
description: The Olympic Run in Děčín is a traditional regional race held at the confluence of the Elbe and Ploučnice rivers. The start and finish are located in front of the Kajak Děčín boathouse. The 4.6 km main race route follows a cycle path almost through the city centre, with asphalt and paved surfaces. The event also includes children’s races over distances from 200 to 1,000 metres. Participants can enjoy the beautiful surroundings, with views of Děčín Castle, the Elbe Canyon and lookout towers, while also supporting the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Dřevěnice
description: The Olympic Run in Dřevěnice is a traditional regional running race with a course of approximately five kilometres. It starts with a challenging climb into the forest above the Dolánky part of the municipality, then heads to a pond, where the course continues on flat asphalt roads, crossing the main road. The finish is at the volleyball courts, which have full facilities. The race is suitable for adults and children, with shorter children’s races ranging from 50 to 1,200 metres. The race starts at 18:00, and registration is available online only until 5 June 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Háj ve Slezsku
description: The Olympic Run in Háj ve Slezsku is part of the nationwide Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values. The event offers courses for adults and children, including a shorter 4 km and a longer 8 km course for adults, as well as children’s races ranging from 60 to 1,000 metres. The start is at the school sports grounds of ZŠ Háj ve Slezsku, and the event has a welcoming atmosphere, with the opportunity to donate to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online, and the event is suitable for the general public, who can enjoy a route through the village and around the athletics track.

name: Olympijský běh - Havířov
description: The Olympic Run in Havířov is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place on June 17, 2026, and offers a 5 km course in the Moravian-Silesian Region. The main category starts at 18:00 by the Na Vyhlídce non-alcoholic bar in Havířov. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate the sporting day with a run.

name: Olympijský běh - Hluboké Mašůvky
description: The Olympic Run in Hluboké Mašůvky is part of the nationwide Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values such as friendship, fair play and respect. The event offers a 5 km adult race and children’s races of 100, 200 and 300 metres. The start is at the football pitch in Hluboké Mašůvky. The main race begins at 18:00 and is started live on Český rozhlas. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. Toilets, a changing room, a baggage storage area and showers are available, and children can enjoy a bouncy castle.

name: Olympijský běh - Holešov
description: The Olympic Run in Holešov is the country’s largest running event, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place in the beautiful setting of the château gardens in Holešov and offers a mixed 5 km race. The main category starts at 18:00, making it an enjoyable evening run for the general public and athletes alike. The event is part of the broader running movement of the Czech Athletics Federation, which promotes running and a healthy lifestyle.

name: Olympijský běh - Holetín
description: The Olympic Run in Holetín returns after a break with a varied route along roads, paved paths, meadows and field trails. The race is open to adults and children, and by taking part you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The start and registration are at the Holetín swimming pool complex, which also has basic amenities. The race starts at 18:00, announced on Czech Radio, and online registration is available until 5 June 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Horní Jelení
description: The Olympic Run in Horní Jelení is a traditional running race with a beautiful route through the local forest and around Pětinoha Pond. It offers races for adults and children, including a 6 km race for adults and shorter 2.5 km and 500 m races for children in different age categories. The race takes place at Komenského Square and starts at 18:00. The atmosphere is friendly, and the event supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online, and the race is timed using chip timing.

name: Olympijský běh - Horoměřice
description: The Olympic Run in Horoměřice offers a 7 km running course completed in two laps. The route is mostly dirt and gravel, with sections of paving stones and concrete slabs. Two-thirds of each lap run gently downhill, while the final third challenges runners with an uphill stretch. Horoměřice is hosting the Olympic Run for the sixth time, and part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The race is suitable for adults and children, with shorter 500 m and 1,000 m races for children.

name: Olympijský běh - Hradec Králové
description: The Olympic Run in Hradec Králové is the country’s largest running event, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place on 17 June 2026, starting at 18:00 near ZŠ Štefánikova, and features a 5 km course. The event is open to the general public and runners of all abilities who want to celebrate this sporting day by running. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Hudčice
description: The Olympic Run in Hudčice is a traditional regional race held on a loop around the village, along paved and dirt roads, including a climb to the quarries above the village. There are also children’s races over 200 and 700 metres. The event is open to all age groups and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only until 5 June 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Chlumec nad Cidlinou
description: The Olympic Run in Chlumec nad Cidlinou is a traditional regional race held on the athletics track by Slavíček Hall. The route follows paved and dirt roads, starting and finishing at the stadium. The race is part of the Olympic Day celebrations, and participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation’s work promoting children’s participation in sport. Alongside the main race for adults, there is also a children’s race, making it possible for the whole family and sports enthusiasts of all ages to take part.

name: Olympijský běh - Chomutov
description: The Olympic Run in Chomutov takes place in the picturesque Bezruč Valley, where the pleasant climate and shade provide ideal conditions for achieving great results. The race features out-and-back road routes with a gentle climb to the turnarounds, rewarding runners in the second half of the race. Both shorter and longer routes are available: 10 km and 5 km, respectively. The event is suitable for the general public and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Chotiměř
description: The Olympic Run in Chotiměř is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place on June 17, 2026, and features a 6 km mixed-surface course starting at the municipal office in Chotiměř. The main category starts at 18:00. The event is suitable for the general public and runners of all levels who want to celebrate the day through running.

name: Olympijský běh - Ivančice
description: The Olympic Run in Ivančice is part of a nationwide celebration of Olympic Day, bringing together athletes of all ages. The adult race runs mostly on sandy terrain along the Jihlava and Rokytná rivers, with natural landmarks at U Šneka and U Dvou bobrů. Children’s races take place on the athletics track, which is also the start and finish venue for the adult races. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. The main race starts at 18:00 at the Ivančice Municipal Stadium.

name: Olympijský běh - Jihlava
location: Letní kino athletic oval, Jihlava, Vysočina, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Jihlava traditionally takes place at the summer cinema venue and athletics track, offering a family-friendly atmosphere full of support and the joy of movement. The race is open to all age groups, with courses for adults and children on mixed terrain. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation, which helps children take part in sports. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is part of the wider Olympic Day, celebrating sport and Olympic values.

name: Olympijský běh - Kamenice
description: The Olympic Run in Kamenice is a traditional regional race that has been held since 2016 in the picturesque Vysočina region. The race offers moderately challenging routes on unpaved paths and asphalt roads around three Kamenice ponds, with a choice of a shorter 2.5 km loop or a longer 5 km loop. Special routes of varying lengths are prepared for children according to age categories. Participants support the Czech Olympic Foundation through their entry fees, helping to promote sports among children. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only until 5 June 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Karviná
description: The Olympic Run in Karviná is a traditional race starting in the historic T. G. Masaryk Square in Karviná-Fryštát. The route passes the Larisch family chateau and through the chateau park, then heads to the city’s landmark, the Darkov Bridge, before returning via the Spa Park to the finish. The race is open to adults and children up to 15 years old, with shorter courses for the children’s races. The event supports the Czech Olympic Foundation and offers a friendly atmosphere, an accompanying programme, and the opportunity for athletes with disabilities to participate in wheelchairs (handbikes).

name: Olympijský běh - Klášterec nad Orlicí
description: The Olympic Run in Klášterec nad Orlicí is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place on the asphalt court by the Sokol Hall and offers 10 km and 5 km courses. The main category starts at 18:00, and the race is suitable for the general public as well as athletes. It is organized by a team of organizers in cooperation with the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Kolín
description: The Olympic Run in Kolín is a traditional sporting event being held for the fourth time as part of the Czech Olympic Committee’s nationwide Olympic Day event. The races take place in the picturesque Borky Forest Park, with two routes: 3 km for adults and 1 km for children. The routes follow forest paths and a cycle path along the Elbe, offering beautiful views and a pleasant running surface. There’s a bouncy castle for children and a photo booth for all participants. The atmosphere is full of sporting spirit and camaraderie. The start and finish are by the bears in Borky Forest Park.

name: Olympijský běh - Kralice nad Oslavou
description: The Olympic Run in Kralice nad Oslavou is a regional running race on a 4 km route along a dirt track and partly on an asphalt road. The race is open to adults and children, with children’s races ranging from 250 to 800 metres. The start is by the football pitch, and the main race begins at 18:00, launched on air by Czech Radio. Participants’ entry fees go to the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online only, until 5 June 2026; registration will not be available on site.

name: Olympijský běh - Krymlov
description: The Olympic Run in Krymlov is a traditional regional race held to celebrate Olympic Day. The event offers a 6.5 km course for adults, as well as children’s races of 200 m and 800 m. The start and registration are in the center of the village by Krymlovská hospoda, where refreshments are available before and after the race. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation, supporting sports development.

name: Olympijský běh - Liberec
description: The Olympic Run in Liberec is a traditional sporting event held at the Sport Park Liberec complex on the inline skating track around the athletics stadium. It offers races for children and adults, with distances from 150 metres up to 6 km, suitable for the general public, including wheelchair users and handbike riders. The main race starts at 18:00. Registration is online only, with the option to register multiple runners at once. The programme also includes a group warm-up and facilities with toilets, changing rooms, showers and a baggage storage area. The entry fee supports the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Líbeznice
description: The Olympic Run in Líbeznice is a new addition to this traditional sporting event, which brings together runners of all ages. The races take place at Areál zdraví, which offers modern sports facilities in the peaceful, leafy surroundings of the village, known for its interesting architectural features. The routes follow asphalt, paved and unpaved paths through the village and surrounding area, including the Mratínka trail, which was created from a former railway spur. The event is not only a sporting occasion but also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation and enjoy a friendly atmosphere and the joy of movement.

name: Olympijský běh - Lovosice
description: The Olympic Run in Lovosice is part of the country’s largest running event, which kicks off Olympic Day celebrations at 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race takes place at the athletics stadium in Lovosice and offers 8 km and 4 km courses. The main category starts at 18:00, and the race is open to runners of all abilities and sports enthusiasts. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletics Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Mělník
description: The Olympic Run in Mělník is a traditional race held amid the picturesque natural landscape of the Elbe Lowlands, around the Elbe River and Na Polabí Park. The children’s races take place on unpaved paths in the park, while adults run along a paved asphalt cycle path with no elevation gain. The event is suitable for the general public and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and registration is online only until June 5, 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Město Touškov
description: The Olympic Run in Město Touškov is a traditional regional race that passes through the town’s historic centre, by the Baroque Church of St. John the Baptist and the Touškov pond. The course combines grass and asphalt surfaces and offers an enjoyable run through picturesque surroundings. The race is open to adults and children, with several course distances, and also supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The start and registration are at the TJ Sokol sports complex. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio.

name: Olympijský běh - Most
description: The Olympic Run in Most takes place in the Matylda recreation area and offers two routes for adults—a shorter 4 km and a longer 8 km course—along the paved inline skating path around Lake Matylda. The race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Český rozhlas radio. Participants’ entry fees support the Czech Olympic Foundation. Registration is online only until June 6; registration will not be available on site. Showers, toilets, a changing room and a baggage storage facility are available for runners. Parking is available in the Matylda area.

name: Olympijský běh - Olomouc
organizer: Český olympijský výbor a Klub vytrvalostních sportů Olomouc
description: The Olympic Run in Olomouc is part of the T-Mobile Olympic Run and offers a bronze-level race with a charitable dimension. The event takes place in Olomouc-Hejčín and includes a 5 km adult race and free children’s races for children up to 15 years old. The race starts at 6 p.m., with the start broadcast on Czech Radio. The entry fee includes a race pack with a sports bag and gifts from partners, and part of the fee goes to support the Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Opava Suché Lazce
description: The Olympic Run in Opava-Suché Lazce is the country’s largest running event, kicking off Olympic Day celebrations at more than 90 locations across the Czech Republic. The race covers a 5 km course and is open to the general public and sports enthusiasts alike. It starts at the municipal football pitch at 18:00, and the event has a friendly, motivating atmosphere for all runners. It is organized by a team of organizers under the auspices of the Czech Athletic Federation.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrava Hošťálkovice
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrava-Hošťálkovice is a traditional running race on paved paths over rolling terrain. It offers two routes for adults—a longer 10 km route and a shorter 5 km route—with the start at the sports complex by ZŠ Výhledy-Hošťálkovice. Children may also take part with permission from a legal guardian, and the event contributes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio. Toilets, changing rooms, showers, and parking are available by MŠ Výhledy.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrava Komenského sady
location: Komenského sady, Ostrava, Moravian-Silesian Region, Czech Republic
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrava’s Komenský Gardens is a traditional sporting event held in a beautiful park along the Ostravice River. The race offers routes for adults and children. The main race starts at 18:00 and is broadcast on Czech Radio. By taking part, participants contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children’s participation in sport. Registration is online, and the race is suitable for the general public, including wheelchair users and handbikes.

name: Olympijský běh - Ostrov u Karlových Varů
description: The Olympic Run in Ostrov near Karlovy Vary is part of Olympic Day, which celebrates sport and Olympic values. The race takes place in the pleasant surroundings of the castle park and follows a sandy path. Participants can run the 5 km course, and online registration is open until 5 June 2026. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is suitable for the general public, including children accompanied by an adult.

name: Olympijský běh - Palkovice
description: The Olympic Run in Palkovice is a traditional regional race held in beautiful surroundings, with a combination of paved roads, forest paths and terrain. The adult course is approximately 5,100 metres long and includes a hill, adding interest and challenge to the race. Children can take part in races over 200 m, 400 m and 1,600 m, making it an event for the whole family. The event is also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation and enjoy a sporting atmosphere in the community. The start and registration are behind the gym in Palkovice; the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Olympijský běh - Pardubice
description: The Olympic Run in Pardubice is a traditional race held in the Studánka forest park. The 3.8 km course runs mainly along forest paths with some asphalt sections and is suitable for beginners thanks to its mostly flat terrain with a few climbs. The event also includes 1.1 km children’s races. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation, and can choose to register with or without a T-shirt.

name: Olympijský běh - Pelhřimov
description: The Olympic Run in Pelhřimov is a traditional running race held in a picturesque town on the edge of the Bohemian-Moravian Highlands. The race offers courses for children and adults, including a longer 7.2 km route and a shorter 4.8 km route, which run through the town parks and surrounding area. The start is at the Senior Citizens’ Home on Radětínská Street, and the race supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. Online registration is available, with the option to sign up multiple runners at once. Pelhřimov is also known for its historic landmarks and Festival of Records and Curiosities, giving the race a unique atmosphere.

name: Olympijský běh - Praha Královka
description: The Olympic Run in Prague – Královka is part of the nationwide celebration of Olympic Day, bringing together sports enthusiasts of all ages. The race offers adult runners a challenging 3.8 km course that runs mainly on paved paths through the park, with some unpaved sections, including stairs and uneven terrain. Shorter distances of 350 m, 550 m and 1,100 m are available for children. By taking part, you contribute to the Czech Olympic Foundation, which supports children with limited financial means in pursuing sport. The main race starts at 18:00. Registration is online only and is open until 5 June 2026.

name: Olympijský běh - Praha Satalice
description: The Olympic Run in Prague-Satalice is a 5 km race that runs mainly along forest trails in the Satalice Game Reserve, a chestnut-lined avenue, and gravel paths in the forest park. The route is flat and offers runners a pleasant setting, with views over fields and a course that passes the Chapel of St. Anne. A warm-up is provided before the start, and motivational announcements are made during the race. After the race, refreshments, showers, changing rooms, and a bag storage area are available, all in a friendly atmosphere. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Rožnov pod Radhoštěm
description: The Olympic Run in Rožnov pod Radhoštěm is part of the largest running event in the Czech Republic, which is being held for the 40th year. On race day, June 17, sports enthusiasts of all ages can enjoy running and other physical activities. The event is also open to sports clubs and associations, which can organize their own Olympic Day. Registration is available only online on the official website until June 5, with the best entry fee for adults available until the end of March.

name: Olympijský běh - Rychnov nad Kněžnou
description: The Olympic Run in Rychnov nad Kněžnou is returning to the running calendar after a long break and invites all runners to celebrate Olympic Day through movement. The main adult race is 5 km long and starts at the swimming pool complex in Včelné. Children can take part in races from 200 m to 1,500 m, depending on their age category. The event also offers an accompanying program, the chance to try SPARTAN obstacles, and facilities including a bag drop, toilets, and showers. Registration is online, with the option to sign up multiple runners at once, and the entry fee contributes to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Strakonice
description: The Olympic Run in Strakonice is a traditional sporting event being held for the third time at the Podskalí campsite. The race offers routes for adults and children, with adults running 4 km on a mix of natural and paved paths. Children can take part in races of 350 m and 1.2 km, accompanied by an Olympic-themed programme. The main race starts at 18:00, and part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation. The event is suitable for all age groups and promotes the joy of movement and a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Stříbro
description: The Olympic Run in Stříbro is a traditional running race that takes place mostly along forest paths and supports Olympic ideals and the Czech Olympic Foundation. The program includes a 5 km race for adults and children’s races of 600 and 1,000 metres. The event is held at the TJ Baník Stříbro stadium and offers a pleasant sporting environment, with online registration available. The main race starts at 18:00. Participants have access to changing rooms, toilets, showers and storage. The race is also open to athletes with disabilities using wheelchairs (handbikes).

name: Olympijský běh - Tachov
description: The Olympic Run in Tachov gives runners the chance to take on a mixed course combining natural and asphalt sections along the Mže River. The race is open to both children aged 15 and under and adults, with a capacity of 100 adult and 100 child participants. The start and registration are at the Tachov Sports Complex – Rychta. The main race starts at 18:00 and is started live on Czech Radio. Registration is online only until June 7; on-site registration will not be available. By purchasing an entry, you contribute CZK 20 to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Tlučeň
description: The Olympic Run in Tlučeň offers a run along forest trails through the České středohoří hills, around Plešivec, with approximately 180 metres of elevation gain—one of the highest elevation gains among Olympic Runs. The route is shaded and is open to adults and children, with shorter courses for the children’s races. The event is part of Olympic Day and supports the Czech Olympic Foundation. The main race starts at 18:00, and the accompanying programme includes, for example, an aikido demonstration. Online registration is open until 5 June 2026; registration will not be available on site.

name: Olympijský běh - Trutnov
description: After last year’s debut, the Olympic Run in Trutnov returns for its second edition. The race offers a 5 km route with mixed terrain, starting at the athletics stadium and passing the swimming pool before following forest paths along the Poříčský Ridge, with the finish back at the stadium. Children’s races of 100 to 800 metres will take place in the stadium grounds. The event is not only a sporting challenge but also an opportunity to support a good cause, as part of the entry fee goes to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Tuhaň
description: The Olympic Run in Tuhan is a traditional race held in the beautiful Kokořínsko Protected Landscape Area. The route runs mainly through forests and meadows, with part of it on an asphalt road, offering a pleasant running experience in nature. The event also includes children’s races on the football pitch, making it suitable for the whole family. The main race starts at 18:00, and the event is also an opportunity to support the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Ústí nad Labem
description: The Olympic Run in Ústí nad Labem is a traditional running race held in the beautiful surroundings of Lake Milada. The race offers routes for adults and children, with a choice of shorter or longer routes for adults. The start is near the car park above Lake Milada’s main beach, and the route follows the water before climbing gently to the finish. Part of the entry fee is donated to the Czech Olympic Foundation to support children’s participation in sport. The race is suitable for the general public who want to enjoy being active and support a good cause.

name: Olympijský běh - Valašské Klobouky
description: The Olympic Run in Valašské Klobouky is a traditional sporting event held in the beautiful, hilly landscape of the White Carpathians. The race offers two main routes for adults—a 5-kilometre and a 10-kilometre course—run mostly on asphalt. Children’s races are also held in the enclosed area of the football pitch. The start is at the TJ Spartak Valašské Klobouky football pitch, and participants make a donation to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Olympijský běh - Vnorovy
description: The Olympic Run in Vnorovy is a traditional regional race on a 6.5 km course along local roads, field tracks and forest paths. Part of the route runs between the Morava River and the Baťa Canal, including a crossing over the Baťa Canal lock. The start and finish are on the athletics track at the Vnorovy sports complex. The race is open to adults and children, with shorter children’s races ranging from 100 to 1,000 metres. Participants make a contribution to the Czech Olympic Foundation.

name: Volksbank Stadtlauf Selm 2026
location: Campus Selm, Selm, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Volksbank Stadtlauf Selm is taking place for the fourth time as part of the popular town festival weekend. The officially measured course runs through the beautiful Auenpark and is popular with athletes from Selm and the surrounding region. The event offers races for various age groups, from Bambini races to fun runs over 5 and 10 kilometres. Mayor Thomas Orlowski will take part in the 10-kilometre race himself, highlighting the event’s friendly, sporting atmosphere.
course_highlights: Officially measured course through the Auenpark
Various races for children, teenagers and adults
Start and finish at Campus Selm
additional: The Stadtlauf begins with the Bambini race at 16:00 in the stadium (400 m). This is followed by school races over 1 km and 2.5 km, as well as fun runs over 5 km (18:00) and 10 km (19:00). Award ceremonies take place between the races. Volksbank Selm-Bork eG is the event’s main sponsor. Several race distances, start in the Auenpark, children’s and youth races, registration now open

name: Olympijský běh - Lelekovice
description: The Olympic Run in Lelekovice is a traditional race held on Olympic Day. The routes run mostly along field and forest paths, with gently rolling terrain and a steep climb before the finish. The main race is 5 km and is suitable for adults and children, while the children’s races cover shorter distances of 150 to 1,060 metres. After the race, prizes are awarded not only to the winners but also to runners selected by draw and older participants, followed by a get-together around a fire with music and the option to roast food. Online registration is open until 5 June 2026, and the main race starts at 18:00.

name: Komořany – Čihadlo
description: Komořany - Čihadlo is a 4.88 km running race with 175 metres of elevation gain, held entirely on forest and field paths. The finish is at the summit of Čihadlo. The race is part of the Hill Running Series in Prague and the surrounding area, offering runners an enjoyable experience in a natural setting on a more challenging course.

name: Běh okolo Špilberku
description: The Run Around Špilberk is a traditional running race in Brno, featuring an interesting course around Špilberk Castle. The race is open to men, women, and children of all ages and takes place in the pleasant early evening. Men run five 1.3 km laps, women run three laps, and the lap length for children is adjusted according to age. Refreshments and a baggage drop-off are available after the race. The affordable entry fee is 150 CZK, and registration takes place at the venue before the race.

name: Radimovický koňák
description: Radimovický koňák is a traditional cross-country race held in the village of Radimovice u Želče, attracting runners of all ages every year. The race takes place in the pleasant surroundings of South Bohemia and offers everyone from the youngest children to adult men, who make up the largest category, the chance to test their strength. The event has a long-standing tradition and is a popular sporting occasion in the region.

name: 44. Heiligenröder Abendlauf
price_range: modest registration fees, free for Bambinis
description: The 44th Heiligenröder Evening Run is a traditional night road race in Niestetal, Germany, and part of the Nordhessencup running series. The event offers distances for all ages and ability levels, from 400 m for Bambinis to 20.35 km for experienced runners. It combines competitive racing with more relaxed running options: Bambinis, walkers and Nordic walkers are timed but not ranked. Participation is free for Bambinis, while children, teenagers and adults pay moderate entry fees.
course_highlights: Night road race in Niestetal-Heiligenrode
Distances from 400 m to 20.35 km
Part of the Nordhessencup running series
additional: Bambinis run for free; entry fees for children, teenagers and adults are moderate. Bambinis, walkers and Nordic walkers are timed but not ranked. The event is listed on laufen.de. Typical June weather: approx. 23 °C, mostly sunny. Night race, multiple distances, events for all ages, part of the Nordhessencup running series.

name: Gänseliesellauf
location: Krischerstraße, Monheim am Rhein, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
organizer: Stadt Monheim am Rhein, Sportgemeinschaft Monheim 1894/1968 e.V.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: inklusive 100 Meter-Lauf für alle keine Anmeldegebühr

description: The 40th Gänseliesellauf takes place on June 12, 2026, in Monheim am Rhein and traditionally kicks off the town festival. Five different races are offered for various age groups, ranging from a 900-meter race for kindergarten children to a 10-kilometer race for adults. The event is organized by the City of Monheim am Rhein together with Sportgemeinschaft Monheim 1894/1968 e. V. Alongside the races, it offers a varied program of food and festival activities. The races start and finish on Krischerstraße, and all participants receive certificates that can be downloaded online.
course_highlights: Start and finish on Krischerstraße at number 10
